source.title: Turn-Averaged SAEs for Feature Discovery and Long-Context Attribution
source.authors: Kevin Der; Harish Kamath; Ben Thompson

record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates SAE features as representations and reports specific limits: turn-averaged features lose per-token detail, feature-description rankings depend on the evaluation, and attribution sufficiency differs across architectures. These results refine the claim that SAE features are complete, canonical units.
record.gate_note: The paper does not test toy-model superposition, feature overlap geometry, or whether capacity pressure explains polysemanticity. It does test SAE feature discovery and representation quality on a language model. The induced-persona results in Appendix I are not evidence that those behaviors occur spontaneously; they are not recorded as rows. Attribution-paragraph results concern a downstream application and do not test the claim versions directly.
record.test_reason: This is an SAE methods paper. It assumes SAEs recover interpretable features in Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct and introduces turn-averaged and nested SAEs. It then compares its own architectures with a per-token SAE on description quality, reconstruction and attribution metrics. It does not ask whether superposition holds, whether features are spread across neurons, or whether SAE features are complete or canonical units. Every quantitative row ranks the study's own method against alternatives, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that turn-averaged SAE features describe a turn's high-level characteristics more completely than per-token features, as judged by an LLM and an embedding metric. Per-token max-pooled features remain best at discriminating texts. Turn-averaged features generalize to document-length spans and make attribution graphs compact. A nested SAE gets the highest completeness and replacement scores. They do not draw conclusions about superposition itself.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains BatchTopK SAEs on turn-averaged activations and compares them with per-token and nested SAE architectures. It does not reproduce the toy-model superposition method or measure feature overlap geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: Feature-description evaluation changes with the task and pooling method. Sonnet 4.6 with assistant prefill produces near-chance pairwise coverage judgments (49.1%); the main-text results use Sonnet without prefill. Pairwise coverage and matching results also vary by SAE architecture and pooling.

fits_no_version.finding: Training SAEs on turn-averaged rather than per-token activations, at the same width and k, yields different feature sets on the same model and layer. Qualitative examples show concepts found by one SAE and missed by the other. The authors conclude that reshaping the training signal can steer SAE features toward chosen characteristics.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The features an SAE recovers depend on its training input and objective (span averaging versus per-token), so the dictionary is shaped by method choices. This bears indirectly on V5's canonicity but is not framed or tested as such.

record.problems: Experiments use one 7B-parameter model. Evaluations depend substantially on LLM-generated feature descriptions, summaries, and judgments; the authors note that turn-averaged and per-token autointerp prompts differ. Qualitative examples are hand-selected, and the long-context comparison uses two documents from a pool of around 50. No ground-truth feature benchmark, feature stability analysis, or test of superposition geometry is reported. Several attribution results are shown in figures without numerical values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Appendix I reports many feature rankings from contrastively induced persona rollouts. These are excluded because the relevant behaviors were elicited by explicit persona instructions and the study does not use them as evidence of spontaneous behavior. Per-paragraph attribution shares in Table 2 and the manually selected attribution subgraph in Section 6.3 are downstream attribution-use results rather than direct measures of the claim versions.

untested.parts: No toy models and no geometry or sparsity transitions.
No neuron-level polysemanticity and no capacity analysis.
No measure of how features are spread across neurons. SAE recoverability is assumed rather than tested against a control.
No test of stability across seeds or dictionaries, of canonicity, or of completeness against a benchmark.
No comparison of 1-D and multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T5' with V4 and V5 labels is not justified. The paper's evaluations are architecture comparisons of the authors' own method against baselines, which the rules exclude as tests. All verdict labels are removed. The study is by Anthropic authors and is a preprint. Judge sensitivity matters: Sonnet with prefill gives near-chance pairwise judgments, 49.1% versus 83.1% without prefill. This affects the description-quality rows but not any claim version.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, more features than dimensions, overlapping nearly orthogonal directions, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether neuron polysemanticity results from competition for limited capacity or whether feature importance determines dedicated versus shared dimensions.
Alternative causes of polysemantic neurons and whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.

The study evaluates SAE feature descriptions and coverage on Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct, but does not measure feature distribution across neurons or establish that the recovered features are the model's underlying features.
It measures reconstruction and attribution sufficiency, but does not test whether SAE features are stable across training runs or canonical across dictionaries and methods.
No comparison of one-dimensional features with multi-dimensional features.

relation.reason: Interpretable SAE features are used as tools for turn-level analysis; the study does not independently test superposition or the completeness, stability or canonicity of dictionary features.

tranche.reason: The study uses SAE feature extraction to develop turn-averaged and nested architectures and evaluates their description, reconstruction and attribution performance. These method comparisons do not test a listed claim version.

source_check.notes: All 20 sampled rows match the source. They describe method evaluations rather than tests of the claim versions, so versions=none and cannot_determine are appropriate; no statements or verdict labels were listed.
